rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī resumes the opening argument: humanity divides into those for whom the throne-bearing angels seek forgiveness—the repentant followers of Islam—and those condemned as unbelievers in divine oneness.
rows.anchor: عاد إلى بدء الكلام الذي أشار فيه إلى أن تنزيل الكتاب وإقامة الدعوة لمغفرة جمع وقبول توبتهم وعقاب آخرين فذكر أن الناس قبال هذه الدعوة قبيلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān does not identify the throne-bearers or explicitly call them angels; the phrase “those around it,” together with 39:75, implies that they too are angels.
rows.anchor: ولم يعرف سبحانه هؤلاء الحاملين للعرش من هم؟ ولا في كلامه تصريح بأنهم من الملائكة لكن يشعر عطف قوله { ومن حوله } عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The throne is where divine commands appear and rulings issue to govern the world; those surrounding it are the angels nearest to God.
rows.anchor: العرش الذي منه تظهر الأوامر وتصدر الأحكام الإلهية التي بها يدبر العالم، والذين حول العرش من الملائكة وهم المقربون منهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels glorify God while praising Him: they deny every attribute unworthy of His holiness, including a partner in His dominion, and praise His acts and governance.
rows.anchor: ينزهون الله سبحانه والحال أن تنزيههم له يصاحب ثناءهم لربهم فهم ينزهونه تعالى عن كل ما لا يليق بساحة قدسه ومن ذلك وجود الشريك في ملكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their belief in God means affirming His oneness in lordship and divinity; mentioning the throne and the angels' testimony rebuts polytheists who worship angels as divine partners.
rows.anchor: معناه الإيمان بوحدانيته في ربوبيته وألوهيته ففي ذكر العرش ونسبة التنزيه والتحميد والإيمان إلى الملائكة رد للمشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They ask forgiveness for those who believe” means that the angels ask God to forgive the believers.
rows.anchor: أي يسألون الله سبحانه أن يغفر للذين آمنوا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels begin their supplication by praising God's encompassing mercy and knowledge: mercy is the source of every blessing to the needy, while knowledge knows each recipient's need and readiness.
rows.anchor: وإنما ذكروا الرحمة وشفعوها بالعلم لأنه برحمته ينعم على كل محتاج فالرحمة مبدأ إفاضة كل نعمة، وبعلمه يعلم حاجة كل محتاج مستعد للرحمة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The followed path is the religion God prescribed, Islam; repentance is returning to God through belief in His oneness and applying that path, and protection from Hell is forgiveness's end and aim.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالسبيل التي اتبعوها هو ما شرع لهم من الدين وهو الإسلام واتباعهم له هو تطبيق عملهم عليه فالمراد بتوبتهم رجوعهم إليه تعالى بالإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers' request for what God promised through His messengers illustrates asking God to grant His promised favor; the cited supplication also asks not to be disgraced on Resurrection Day.
rows.anchor: ربنا وآتنا ما وعدتنا على رسلك ولا تخزنا يوم القيامة إنك لا تخلف الميعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has made acceptance of repentance a duty upon Himself and a right for repentants, as stated in 4:17.
rows.anchor: وقبول التوبة مما أوجبه الله تعالى على نفسه وجعله حقا للتائبين عليه قال تعالى إنما التوبة على الله للذين يعملون السوء بجهالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Requesting forgiveness for repentants, whose right God has pledged to grant, is in truth asking Him to fulfill His promise and expressing eagerness for His favor.
rows.anchor: فطلب كل حق أوجبه الله تعالى على نفسه منه كسؤال المغفرة للتائب هو في الحقيقة رجوع إليه لاستنجاز ما وعده وإظهار اشتياق للفوز بكرامته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even a divine act that must occur remains a favor: no other agent compels God, who affects everything; He obligates Himself and decrees the gift by His own will. A non-obligatory gift is still more plainly a favor.
rows.anchor: إذ هو المؤثر في كل شيء لا يؤثر فيه غيره بل كان ذلك بإيجاب منه تعالى على نفسه ويؤول معناه إلى قضائه تعالى فعل شيء من الأفعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meeting God means that distracting causes are cut off, God appears as manifest truth, and people are exposed to Him; the author links this wording to 32:10, 11:29, and 84:6.
rows.anchor: ومعنى اللقاء تقطع الأسباب الشاغلة وظهور أن الله هو الحق المبين وبروزهم لله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their becoming manifest to God means imagined causes that drew them to themselves and veiled them from their Lord are removed, so they see His encompassing dominion and exclusive judgment, lordship, and divinity.
rows.anchor: وارتفاع الأسباب الوهمية التي كانت تجذبهم إلى نفسها وتحجبهم عن ربهم وتغفلهم عن إحاطة ملكه وتفرده في الحكم وتوحده في الربوبية والالوهية.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Nothing of them is hidden from God” explains their exposure: hearts, deeds, outward and inward states, and what they remembered or forgot are all uncovered.
rows.anchor: فقلوبهم وأعمالهم بعين الله وظاهرهم وباطنهم وما ذكروه وما نسوه مكشوفة غير مستورة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine question and answer about ownership reveal the day's reality: God's dominion and authority over creation appear without restriction; His oneness and subduing power explain why ownership belongs only to Him.
rows.anchor: سؤال وجواب من ناحيته سبحانه تبين بهما حقيقة اليوم وهي ظهور ملكه وسلطانه تعالى على الخلق على الإطلاق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every soul receives exactly what it earned, so its recompense is its deed itself; 66:7 likewise says people are repaid for what they did.
rows.anchor: والمراد بيان خصيصة اليوم وهي أن كل نفس تجزى عين ما كسبت فجزاؤها عملها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's swift accounting explains the denial of injustice arising from error: counting one soul does not distract Him from another. Deliberate injustice is already impossible when recompense is the deed itself.
rows.anchor: لا يشغله حساب نفس عن حساب أخرى حتى يخطئ فيجزي نفسا غير جزائها فيظلمها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Āzifa describes the Resurrection as near and imminent; the author cites 70:6–7, where people see it as distant but God sees it as near.
rows.anchor: الآزفة من أوصاف القيامة ومعناها القريبة الدانية قال تعالى إنهم يرونه بعيدا ونراه قريبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearts being at throats is a metaphor for extreme fear, as though hearts leave their places and rise to the throats; “throats” means the outward top of the windpipe.
rows.anchor: الحناجر جمع حنجرة وهي رأس الغلصمة من خارج وكون القلوب لدى الحناجر كناية عن غاية الخوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kāẓimīn derives from constraint or suppression and means being intensely distressed.
rows.anchor: وكاظمين من الكظم وهو شدة الاغتمام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ḥamīm is a close relative, but no relative can defend the wrongdoers through kinship; 23:101 denies family ties on that Day, and no intercessor will be obeyed for them.
rows.anchor: الحميم القريب أي ليس لهم قريب يقوم بنصرهم بحمية القرابة قال تعالى فلا أنساب بينهم يومئذ المؤمنون 101، ولا شفيع يطاع في شفاعته.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One grammatical explanation treats “the eye's treachery” as a verbal noun like “treachery,” “lying,” and “frivolous speech”; it means hidden eye-sins, such as a furtive glance, not every eye-sin, as the pairing with concealed hearts indicates.
rows.anchor: قيل الخائنة مصدر كالخيانة نظيرة الكاذبة واللاغية بمعنى الكذب واللغو، وليس المراد بخائنة الأعين كل معصية من معاصيها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation makes “treacherous eyes” an adjective-noun construction and takes God's knowledge here to mean recognizing the treacherous eyes.
rows.anchor: وقيل { خائنة الأعين } من قبيل إضافة الصفة إلى الموصوف، ولازمه كون العلم بمعنى المعرفة والمعنى يعرف الأعين الخائنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī prefers the first explanation: “the eye's treachery” is a verbal noun for covert glances, not the adjective-noun reading.
rows.anchor: والوجه هو الأول.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What breasts conceal is what the soul keeps hidden: forms of unbelief, hypocrisy, and sin.
rows.anchor: وهو ما تسره النفس وتستره من وجوه الكفر والنفاق وهيئات المعاصي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's judging truly, while those invoked apart from Him judge nothing, is another proof of His exclusive divinity, set up after His sole sovereignty and knowledge of hidden glances and hearts.
rows.anchor: هذه حجة أخرى على توحده تعالى بالألوهية أقامها بعد ما ذكر حديث انحصار الملك فيه يوم القيامة وعلمه بخائنة الأعين وما تخفي الصدور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Judgment among servants is essential to divinity: God judges creation on Resurrection Day, whereas those invoked besides Him cannot judge because they are owned servants with no ownership.
rows.anchor: من اللازم الضروري في الألوهية أن يقضي الإله في عباده وبينهم والله سبحانه هو يقضي بين الخلق وفيهم يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar transmits from the Prophet that remorse suffices as repentance and a believer rejoices at good and grieves at sin; lack of remorse means no faith or intercession and makes the sinner an oppressor.
rows.anchor:
قال النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
" كفى بالندم توبة "

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Asked about “the eye's treachery,” Abū ʿAbd Allāh explains it as a man looking at something while appearing not to look.
rows.anchor: سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام عن قول الله عز وجل { يعلم خائنة الأعين } فقال ألم تر إلى الرجل ينظر إلى الشيء وكأنه لا ينظر

rows.speaker: سعد
rows.claim: Saʿd reports that at Mecca's conquest the Prophet granted safety except to four men and two women, including ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Sarḥ; after Uthmān sought his pledge, the Prophet said a prophet must not signal secretly with his eyes.
rows.anchor: عن سعد قال لما كان يوم فتح مكة أمن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم الناس إلا أربعة نفر وامرأتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This passage returns to the disbelievers' rejection of the Qurʾān and their plot to defeat its proof, then describes consequences for unbelievers and the good end of the steadfast.
rows.anchor: بيان رجوع إلى حديث كفرهم بالقرآن المذكور في أول السورة وذكر كيدهم لإبطال حجته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laghw is something baseless in affairs or meaningless in speech; the verb laghā means to produce such nonsense.
rows.anchor: اللغو من الأمر ما لا أصل له ومن الكلام ما لا معنى له يقال لغى يلغي ويلغو لغوا أي أتى باللغو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their explicit reference to “this Qurʾān,” while naming it, shows how intensely they focused on it in trying to erase its effect.
rows.anchor: والإشارة إلى القرآن مع ذكر اسمه دليل على كمال عنايتهم بالقرآن لإعفاء أثره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order to make noise shows their utter inability to meet the Qurʾān with an equivalent discourse or counterargument; they tried to disrupt the Prophet's recitation so listeners would not hear its verses and be overcome.
rows.anchor: تدل على نهاية عجزهم عن مخاصمة القرآن بإتيان كلام يعادله ويماثله أو إقامة حجة تعارضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in the threat is an oath; in context “those who disbelieved” means the people who urged others not to listen, though the wording is general.
rows.anchor: اللام للقسم، والمراد بالذين كفروا بحسب مورد الآية هم الذين قالوا لا تسمعوا لهذا القرآن وإن كانت الآية مطلقة بحسب اللفظ.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reading strips “worst” of its comparative force: the disbelievers are repaid for the evil deed they used to do.
rows.anchor: قيل المراد العمل السيء الذي كانوا يعملون بتجريد أفعل عن معنى التفضيل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reading says the verse names punishment for their worst deeds and leaves the rest unmentioned to intensify the warning.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بيان جزاء ما هو أسوأ أعمالهم وسكت عن الباقي مبالغة في الزجر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī lists parses for “that is the recompense”: “fire” may appose or explain “that,” be the predicate of an omitted subject (“it is the Fire”), or begin a clause completed by “they have there an abode of eternity.”
rows.anchor: { ذلك جزاء } مبتدأ وخبر و { النار } بدل أو عطف بيان من { ذلك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire surrounds all of them, and each has a distinct abode in it in which to remain forever.
rows.anchor: أي النار محيطة بهم جميعا ولكل منهم فيها دار تخصه خالدا فيها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final “recompense for their denial” can be an absolute object with an understood verb, “they are recompensed a recompense,” or modify the earlier noun “recompense,” as in 17:63.
rows.anchor: وقوله { جزاء بما كانوا بآياتنا يجحدون } مفعول مطلق لفعل مقدر، والتقدير يجزون جزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Hell, the disbelievers ask God to show them the jinn and human leaders who led them astray so they can put them beneath their feet, humiliating them and intensifying their torment.
rows.anchor: يسألون الله أن يريهم متبوعيهم من الجن والإنس ليجعلوهما تحت أقدامهم إذلالا لهما وتشديدا لعذابهما

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib defines istiqāma through the image of a straight, level road, which is used as a metaphor for the path of truth and for a person's adherence to it.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب الاستقامة تقال في الطريق الذي يكون على خط مستو، وبه شبه طريق الحق

rows.speaker: الصحاح
rows.claim: Al-Ṣiḥāḥ gives istiqāma as uprightness or evenness and illustrates it with the expression that a matter became straight.
rows.anchor: وفي الصحاح الاستقامة الاعتدال يقال استقام له الأمر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intended steadfastness is remaining on the middle of the road without deviation and holding firm to one's confession; the different interpretations return to this sense, as illustrated by 9:7 and 42:15.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بقوله { ثم استقاموا } لزوم وسط الطريق من غير ميل وانحراف والثبات على القول الذي قالوه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers' good condition and reward in these verses contrasts with the preceding description of the disbelievers' bad condition.
rows.anchor: والآية وما يتلوها بيان حسن حال المؤمنين كما كانت الآيات قبلها بيان سوء حال الكافرين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels' descent strengthens believers' hearts, reassures them against fear and grief, and brings glad tidings of divine honor and the promised Garden.
rows.anchor: إخبار عما سيستقبلهم به الملائكة من تقوية قلوبهم وتطييب نفوسهم والبشرى بالكرامة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear concerns an anticipated harm, such as punishment or losing Paradise; grief concerns an actual harm, such as sins committed or good things missed. The angels reassure them that sins are forgiven and punishment averted.
rows.anchor: والخوف إنما يكون من مكروه متوقع كالعذاب الذي يخافونه والحرمان من الجنة الذي يخشونه، والحزن إنما يكون من مكروه واقع وشر لازم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise that they “used to be promised” indicates that the angels descend with this good news after earthly life.
rows.anchor: وفي قولهم { كنتم توعدون } دلالة على أن تنزلهم بهذه البشرى عليهم إنما هو بعد الحياة الدنيا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We are your allies in this life and the next” completes the glad tidings: mention of earthly guardianship prepares for the afterlife, whose guardianship follows from their earthly loyalty.
rows.anchor: من تتمة البشارة، وعلى هذا فذكر ولايتهم لهم في الحياة الدنيا مع انقضاء وقتها كما تقدم من باب التوطئة والتمهيد إلى ذكر الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angel guardianship does not conflict with God's being the guardian: angels mediate mercy and honor and have no independent authority.
rows.anchor: وكون الملائكة أولياء لهم لا ينافي كونه تعالى هو الولي لأنهم وسائط الرحمة والكرامة ليس لهم من الأمر شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast with the enemies given demonic companions suggests that these angel allies provide guidance and support; only the guiding angels are specific to God's friends, while angels of guarding, provision, and lifespans serve believers and unbelievers alike.
rows.anchor: وبالمقابلة يستفاد أن المراد ولايتهم لهم بالتسديد والتأييد فإن الملائكة المسددين هم المخصوصون بأهل ولاية الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported alternative takes “we are your allies” as God's speech rather than the angels' speech.
rows.anchor: وقيل الآية من كلام الله دون الملائكة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun “therein” refers to the afterlife. Desire is a strong inclination toward what a faculty wants and enjoys, while asking is broader: every desire is a request, but requests can exceed desires.
rows.anchor: وأصل الإدعاء - وهو افتعال من الدعاء - هو الطلب فالجملة الثانية أعني قوله { ولكم فيها ما تدعون } أوسع نطاقا من الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise grants believers ordinary pleasures such as food, drink, and sex, and also the wider and higher range of whatever they ask for.
rows.anchor: فالآية تبشرهم بأن لهم في الآخرة ما يمكن أن تتعلق به شهواتهم من أكل وشرب ونكاح وغير ذلك بل ما هو أوسع من ذلك وأعلى كعبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-jawārī is the plural of ship; al-aʿlām means signs and is also used for mountains. Ships are likened to mountains because of their size and height.
rows.anchor: الجواري جمع جارية وهي السفينة، والأعلام جمع علم وهو العلامة ويسمى به الجبل وشبهت السفائن بالجبال لعظمها وارتفاعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the subject of “if He wills”; ẓalla means “became,” and rawākid means stationary. God may stop the wind that drives the ships, leaving them still on the sea.
rows.anchor: ضمير { يشأ } لله تعالى، وظل بمعنى صار، و { رواكد } جمع راكدة وهي الثابتة في محلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ships carry people and goods from shore to shore by wind; these are signs for anyone who restrains himself from useless concerns and reflects on God's blessings, since reflection on a blessing is gratitude.
rows.anchor: لآيات لكل من حبس نفسه عن الاشتغال بما لا يعنيه واشتغل بالتفكر في نعمه والتفكر في النعمة من الشكر.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A reported interpretation takes “every patient, grateful person” to mean a believer, who is patient in adversity and grateful in prosperity.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بكل صبار شكور المؤمن لأن المؤمن لا يخلو من أن يكون في الضراء أو في السراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yubiq means destroy; its feminine pronoun refers to ships and its masculine pronoun to people. God may drown ships because of people's sins while forgiving many sins, since even some sins suffice to merit destruction.
rows.anchor: الإيباق الإهلاك، وضمير التأنيث للجواري وضمير التذكير للناس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One alternative makes the destruction apply to the passengers, figuratively or by supplying an omitted noun, and takes the clause as God sending destructive winds; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says this reading is strained.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بإهلاكها إهلاك أهلها إما مجازا أو بتقدير مضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects the passenger-destruction reading as strained: it requires construing the clause as God sending storm winds, drowning some people for their sins and saving others by pardon.
rows.anchor: ولا يخفي وجه التكلف فيه.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another alternative coordinates “He pardons” with “He stills the wind,” making God either punish through stillness or violent winds, or pardon many; the author says this is equally strained.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن { يعف } عطف على قوله { يسكن الريح } إلى قوله { بما كسبوا } ولذا عطف بالواو لا بأو،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author likewise calls the second coordination proposal strained.
rows.anchor: وهو في التكلف كسابقه.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The clause about the disputants learning they have no escape is read as a purpose clause coordinated with an omitted purpose, approximately “to show His power”; this construction often occurs in the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: قيل هو غاية معطوفة على أخرى محذوفة، والتقدير نحو من قولنا ليظهر به قدرته ويعلم الذين يجادلون في آياتنا ما لهم من مفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God takes the Prophet away, the phrase means causing him to die before taking vengeance; an alternative says it means removing him from the people's midst.
rows.anchor: المراد بالإذهاب به توفيه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قبل الانتقام منهم، وقيل المراد إذهابه بإخراجه من بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will certainly exact vengeance whether the Prophet dies before it or sees it during his lifetime; “we are powerful over them” means God's power surpasses theirs.
rows.anchor: ومحصل الآية إنا منتقمون منهم بعد توفيك أو قبلها لا محالة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Fa-immā nadhhabanna bika” derives from “if We take you away,” with mā added and the nūn for emphasis.
rows.anchor: أصله إن نذهب بك زيدت عليه ما والنون للتأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to hold fast follows from all that precedes: revelation and prophethood are God's established way, the revealed Book is true, the Prophet is a clear messenger, only the Godfearing respond, and God will punish those who reject it; he is on a straight path.
rows.anchor: فأكد عليه الأمر بعد ذلك كله أن يجد في التمسك بالكتاب الذي أوحي إليه لأنه على صراط مستقيم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent meaning of dhikr is remembrance of God, as elsewhere in this sūrah; the lām marks the obligations addressed to the Prophet and his people, and “you will be asked” supports accountability for them on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن المراد بالذكر ذكر الله، وبهذا المعنى تكرر مرارا في السورة، واللام في { لك ولقومك } للاختصاص بمعنى توجه ما فيه من التكاليف إليهم

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators instead understand dhikr as honor or renown: the Qurʾān is a great distinction by which the Prophet and his Arab people are remembered among nations.
rows.anchor: وعن أكثر المفسرين أن المراد بالذكر الشرف الذي يذكر به، والمعنى وإنه لشرف عظيم لك ولقومك من العرب تذكرون به بين الأمم.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view takes “ask those We sent before you” as asking previous prophets' communities or religious scholars, like 10:94; the author says this is metaphorical because they are asked about the very message their prophets brought.
rows.anchor: قيل المراد بالسؤال منهم السؤال من أممهم وعلماء دينهم كقوله تعالى فسئل الذين يقرأون الكتاب من قبلك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view makes the question refer to the People of the Torah and Gospel: even if they disbelieve, the transmitted testimony establishes the proof; the address is to the Prophet and the duty to his community. The author finds this less plausible for lack of a clear reason to single them out.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد السؤال من أهل الكتابين التوراة والإنجيل فإنهم وإن كفروا لكن الحجة تقوم بتواتر خبرهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third view says the Prophet was told on the Night Journey to ask the assembled spirits of earlier prophets whether they brought any religion beyond monotheism; several reports from the Imams support it.
rows.anchor: وقيل الآية مما خوطب به النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ليلة المعراج أن يسأل أرواح الأنبياء عليهم السلام وقد اجتمع بهم

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: A report from Abū ʿAbd Allāh identifies the enduring word in Abraham's descendants as imamate lasting until the Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: وقيل الكلمة الباقية في عقبه هي الإمامة إلى يوم الدين. عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī notes other reports with this meaning, some applying the verse specifically to imamate among the descendants of al-Ḥusayn.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا المعنى روايات أخر وقد طبقت الآية في بعضها على الإمامة في عقب الحسين عليه السلام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reports make sense if the pronoun in “made it” refers to guidance implied by Abraham's “He will guide me”; the author cites God's appointment of Abraham as an imam and identifies the fullest guidance with imamate.
rows.anchor: والتأمل في الروايات يعطي أن بناءها على إرجاع الضمير في { جعلها } الى الهداية المفهومة من قوله { سيهدين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An imam guides people in the unseen dimension of their deeds, directing them toward God and their proper degrees of nearness; true guidance comes from God and is attributed to the imam only derivatively.
rows.anchor: أن الإمام وظيفته هداية الناس في ملكوت أعمالهم بمعنى سوقهم إلى الله سبحانه بإرشادهم وإيرادهم درجات القرب من الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The descending guidance first fully includes the imam and then flows from him to others; Abraham's absolute guidance fits the imam's highest share, so making it an enduring word means making imamate endure in his descendants.
rows.anchor: فله أتم الهداية ولغيره ما هي دونها وما ذكره إبراهيم عليه السلام في قوله { فإنه سيهدين } هداية مطلقة

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن أمية المخزومي
rows.claim: Abd Allāh ibn Umayya objects that, if God intended to send a messenger, He should choose a wealthier and more eminent man, such as al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra in Mecca or ʿUrwa ibn Masʿūd in Ṭāʾif.
rows.anchor: إذ قال له عبد الله بن أمية المخزومي لو أراد الله أن يبعث إلينا رسولا لبعث أجل من فيما بيننا مالا وأحسنه حالا

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: In his answer, the Prophet explains that God apportions livelihoods so people need one another: the wealthy need the poor's goods, services, knowledge, judgment, or skill, just as the poor need the wealthy's money.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر عليه السلام في كلام طويل جواب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم عن قوله بما في معنى الآيات

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The report says neither a king can demand the poor person's knowledge be joined to his wealth nor a poor person demand the king's wealth be joined to his own knowledge; their needs are complementary.
rows.anchor: ثم ليس للملك أن يقول هلا اجتمع إلى مالي علم هذا الفقير ولا للفقير أن يقول هلا اجتمع إلى رأيي ومعرفتي وعلمي

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet's reported conclusion is that God's mercy is better than the worldly wealth people accumulate.
rows.anchor: ثم قال يا محمد { ورحمة ربك خير مما يجمعون } أي ما يجمعه هؤلاء من أموال الدنيا.

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين
rows.claim: Asked about the verse's hypothetical, ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn says it means that Muhammad's community would all have become unbelievers, united on one religion, if the stated condition had occurred.
rows.anchor: سألت علي بن الحسين عليه السلام عن قول الله عز وجل { ولولا أن يكون الناس أمة واحدة } قال عنى بذلك أمة محمد أن يكونوا
